'''Sandip Chakrabarti''' is an Indian [[astrophysicist]].  He developed a computer model to show how life on earth could have originated in outer space.<ref name="Britt">{{cite web|url=http://www.space.com/scienceastronomy/planetearth/dna_spacegerm_000124.html|title=How Comets Might Seed Planets|last=Britt|first=Robert Roy|date=24 January 2000|publisher=[[Space.com]]|access-date=31 August 2010}}</ref>

==Education==
He started his education in [[Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Vidyamandir]] in [[Malda, West Bengal|Malda]]. After finishing his Bachelor of Science from Ramakrishna Mission Residential College, Narendrapur<ref name="RKM">{{cite web|url=http://www.rkmcnarendrapur.org/index1.php|title=RKM, Narendrapur}}</ref>  in Physics Honours in 1979 (and becoming topper of Calcutta University<ref name="CU">{{cite web|url=http://www.caluniv.ac.in|title=Calcutta University|last=Calcutta University|first= Kolkata}}</ref>) he went to IIT, Kanpur to complete his M.Sc. Degree in Physics in 1981. He joined the Physics Dept. of the [[University of Chicago]] in 1981 to complete PhD work. Soon he completed a paper with Robert Geroch and X.B. Liang on a Theorem on "Time like Curves of limited acceleration in General Relativity",<ref name="Geroch">{{cite journal
|bibcode=1983JMP....24..597C
|doi=10.1063/1.525733
|title=Timelike Curves of Limited Acceleration
|last1=Chakrabarti|first1=Sandip
|last2=Geroch|first2=Robert
|last3=Liang|first3=Can-bin
|date=March 1983
|journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics |pages=597–598
|issue=3
|volume=24
}}</ref> and under S. Chandrasekhar's supervision solved the Dirac equation for massive particles with spin in Kerr geometry.<ref name="Chandra">{{cite journal
|bibcode=1984RSPSA.391...27C
|doi=10.1098/rspa.1984.0002
|title=On Mass-Dependent Spheroidal Harmonics of Spin One-Half
|last=Chakrabarti|first=Sandip
|date=January 1984
|journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London, Series A |pages=27–38
|issue=1800
|volume=391
|s2cid=120673756
}}</ref> 
Subsequently, he concentrated on black hole astrophysics, received his Ph.D. in 1985 and went to [[Caltech]] as a R.C. Tolman Fellow.<ref name="The Telegrph News">{{cite web|url=http://www.telegraphindia.com/1110107/jsp/calcutta/story_13403727.jsp|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130203115553/http://www.telegraphindia.com/1110107/jsp/calcutta/story_13403727.jsp|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 February 2013|title=The Telegraph Newspaper Report|access-date=25 December 2012}}</ref> Major work in this period includes finding Natural Angular Momentum distribution of barotropic flow around black holes,<ref name="skc">{{cite journal
|bibcode=1985ApJ...288....1C
|doi=10.1086/162755
|title=The natural angular momentum distribution in the study of thick disks around black holes
|last=Chakrabarti|first=Sandip
|date=January 1985
|journal=Astrophysical Journal |pages=674–688
|volume=313
}}</ref> nucleosynthesis around black holes.<ref name="Paper, 1985">{{cite journal
|bibcode=1985BAAS...17..856J
|author=Jin, L.
|author2=Arnett, W. D.
|author3=Chakrabarti, S. K.
|title=Detailed Numerical Calculations of Nucleosynthesis in Thick Accretion Disks Around Black Holes
|journal=Bulletin of the American Astronomical Society
|volume=17
|pages=856
|date=September 1985}}</ref><ref name="Dave">{{cite journal
|bibcode=1987ApJ...313..674C 
|doi=10.1086/165006
|title=Nucleosynthesis inside Thick Accretion Disks around a Black Hole. I. Thermodynamic Conditions and Preliminary Analysis
|last1=Chakrabarti|first1=Sandip
|last2=Jin|first2=L.
|last3=Arnett|first3=Arnett, W.D.
|date=February 1987
|journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume=288
|page=674
}}</ref>

==Career==
After a brief period at ICTP, Trieste, where Chakrabarti completed a few definitive work on the formation of shocks in transonic/advective flows around black holes, he joined [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]], and [[S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences|S.N. Bose National Centre]]. Currently, he is  the Director of [[Indian Centre for Space Physics]],<ref name="SKC, ICSP">{{cite web|url=http://csp.res.in/ICSP-WEB/skc.html|title=Webpage of Sandip K Chakrabarti at ICSP website}}</ref> Kolkata, which he founded in 1999. He was at NASA Goddard Space Flight Centre (1994-1995) as a Senior Associate selected by National Research Council.

==Research==
The main focus of Chakrabarti's research is the hydrodynamic and radiative properties of astrophysical flows around black holes and other compact objects. He showed that the accreting matter must be transonic<ref name = "C89">{{cite journal
|bibcode=1989ApJ...347..365C
|doi=10.1086/168125
|title=Standing Rankine-Hugoniot shocks in the hybrid model flows of the black hole accretion and winds
|last=Chakrabarti|first=Sandip
|journal=Astrophysical Journal, Part 1
|date=December 1989
|pages=365–372
|issn=0004-637X
|volume =347}}</ref> and should have standing, oscillating and propagating shocks. He and his collaborators studied many aspects of these flows and showed that the black hole accretion must have non-Keplerian component which plays a major role in deciding the observational properties. He wrote the first monograph on "Theory of Transonic Astrophysical Flows"<ref name="Book 90">{{Cite book |title=Theory of Transonic Astrophysical Flows |publisher = Theory of Transonic Astrophysical Flows. Edited by Chakrabarti Sandip K. Published by World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd|last=Chakrabarti|first=Sandip|date=1990 |isbn=978-981-02-0204-0 |doi = 10.1142/1091|bibcode = 1990ttaf.book.....C}}</ref> (World Scientific Pub. Co., Singapore; 1990). He has completed over 650 research articles and written or edited several books and conference volumes.<ref name="SKC_articles">{{cite web|url=http://csp.res.in/ICSP-WEB/Docs/skc_cv.pdf|title=SKC_biodata.}}</ref> Fifty Nine students have completed Ph.D. Thesis under his supervision.<ref name="SKC_articles"/>

Chakrabarti was the first scientist to suggest that [[Gamma-ray burst]]s are the birth cry of [[black holes]] at his presentation in 1995, third Huntsville, Alabama Conference.<ref name="Birth Cry">{{cite conference |url=http://www.batse.msfc.nasa.gov/events/3hgrbs/abstracts/models.html |title=ARE GAMMA RAY BURSTS THE 'BIRTH CRY' OF BLACK HOLES? |id=M-P17 |last=Chakrabarti |first=Sandip |date=1995 |conference=3rd Huntsville Symposium on Gamma-Ray Bursts |location=Hunsville, Alabama |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130302201548/http://www.batse.msfc.nasa.gov/events/3hgrbs/abstracts/models.html |archive-date=2 March 2013 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> In 2013, Scientists observed a conclusive evidence of this birth cry.<ref name="HT">{{cite web|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Kolkata/Indian-scientist-first-to-record-birth-cry-of-black-hole/Article1-986905.aspx|title=Hindustan Times Link|last=Chakrabarti|first=Sandip|date=January 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130112002419/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Kolkata/Indian-scientist-first-to-record-birth-cry-of-black-hole/Article1-986905.aspx|archive-date=2013-01-12}}</ref> He is also the first to suggest (1992-1996) that the [[accretion disk]]s in an extreme mass ratio binaries could change the [[gravitational wave]] signals.<ref name="extreme">{{cite journal
|bibcode=1996PhRvD..53.2901C
|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.53.2901
|title=Gravitational wave emission from a binary black hole system in the presence of an accretion disk
|author=Chakrabarti, Sandip K.
|journal =Physical Review D
|date=March 1996
|volume=53
|issue= 6
|pages=2901–2907
|pmid=10020290
|arxiv=astro-ph/9603117
|s2cid=36096244
}}</ref>
